# Working of Fibonacci Series

#### Course: Learn Recursion With Java

## Working of Fibonacci Series

The code of the Fibonacci series was easy to write. However, its working could be tricky to understand.

In the Fibonacci Series,

```java
nth element = (n - 1)th element + (n - 2)th element
```

Let's calculate the number at the fifth position in the Fibonacci series, fib(4):

```java
fib(4) = fib(3) + fib(2)
```

So, fib(4) calls fib(3) and fib(2).

![Method Calls Made By fib(4)](data:image/png;base64,)

Again, fib(3) requires two values: fib(2) and fib(1).

![Method Calls Made By fib(3)](data:image/png;base64,)

Similarly, fib(2) requires fib(1) and fib(0).

![Method Calls Made By fib(2)](data:image/png;base64,)

Now, fib(1) and fib(0) being the base cases, they return 1 and 0 respectively.

![Return Values of fib(1) and fib(0)](data:image/png;base64,)

Once the base conditions return their values, each preceding call also starts returning values as shown in the figure below.

![Working of the fib() Method](data:image/png;base64,)

Here, you can see the sequence of method calls in the Fibonacci series is not linear but forms a tree-like structure.
